title: Human-Written Resumes Beat AI in Job-Hunt Test
paragraphs: Many job seekers now use artificial intelligence (AI) to write their resumes. But a new experiment suggests that a resume written by a person may still get better results.

The experiment was carried out by Kickresume, a company that makes online tools to help people write resumes. Over two months in 2026, the company sent 204 job applications to real job openings in the US. Most of the jobs were in customer service and sales.

The company used four different versions of a resume, and it sent each version 51 times. The results were very different. A simple resume written by a person, with all the information in one column, did the best. It got a positive response 31% of the time. A resume written by a person in two columns got a response rate of only 12%.

The AI resumes did not do as well. A resume made by AI without any changes was the weakest, with a response rate of just 10%. However, when the AI resume was changed to match each job, the response rate almost doubled to 18%.

Kickresume said the results should be treated with care. The different resumes were not sent to the same jobs at the same time. For example, the best resume was sent first, to the jobs that matched it best. This may explain part of its success. Because of this, the company said the results are signals, not proof.
The experiment also showed that companies often reply quickly. More than four in ten replies came within one day, and about eight in ten came within three days.
